title: Dave Canales: 'The Lights Will Never Be Too Bright for Those Two'
headline: Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan's connection came alive under the lights after a rough practice week, Chuba Hubbard's run game got going, and Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and Monroe Freeling left the game with unclear status.
summary: Canales praised the Bank of America Stadium crowd for forcing false starts on Detroit and fueling a defense that had to get back on the field several times. He said the RPO game gave the offense balance and optionality, letting the team dictate man or zone looks and hit deep shots when Detroit played man, including a big McMillan touchdown. He described a difficult practice week for Young and McMillan, with misses they had to talk through, and said that struggle made the Sunday night success more rewarding and reinforced not judging a week early. He called McMillan's catch a clean one with both feet in. On defense he credited the communication of Nick Scott, who is back from injury, and said the week's practice was the unit's best in run and pass concepts. He praised Chuba Hubbard for breaking tackles and running with the right attitude, with play-action helping the run game. Monroe Freeling could not finish the game and will get a full evaluation. Jaelan Phillips appears to have a hamstring issue and could not return; the severity is unknown. Canales also said the upcoming week-five bye is useful for getting several injured players back and for evaluating the first quarter of the season.

title: Ben Johnson pleased with defense’s performance vs. Jets | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams is out for Week 5 at Green Bay, Kyle Monangai has a day-to-day thumb injury, and Roschon Johnson may see more goal-line work.
summary: Ben Johnson opened by praising the coaches and players for finding a 3-1 start and for the effort in the win over the Jets, while stressing that execution in all three phases still needs work. He defended Tyson Bagent, who had two interceptions negated and is now the starter, saying Bagent made good decisions and that the ball-security coaching is about balancing caution with aggression. Johnson said Kyle Monangai's thumb is expected to be fine and is a day-to-day issue. He said Caleb Williams is rehabbing well but will not play this week, and that his status is still week to week. On the defense, Johnson praised Dayo Odeyingbo's high-effort play as an interior rusher and credited better rush integrity and coverage windows for the third-down improvement. On red zone struggles, he said the issues vary week to week, with last week's problems tied to negative plays and this week's to detail, and he said Friday's red zone practice will be used to fix them. He suggested Roschon Johnson, with a bigger frame, could help near the goal line. Johnson said Theo Benedet's play at tackle was encouraging, and that the offense's core approach doesn't change much regardless of which quarterback is playing. Johnson described Jahdae Walker-style... no further detail, and said Swift's role for the coming week will be determined in practice after his fumble.

title: HC Sean Payton on deciding Week 4 plays: 'Those guys made ‘em'
headline: Payton says the offense needs to fix its slow start and Courtland Sutton's role, while RJ Harvey's ten-catch day drew praise for some big plays.
summary: Payton called the loss a tight game that turned on a few plays, including a turnover in the kicking game that flipped field position. He said the offense had only about 30 yards at halftime and needs to improve quickly before Week 5. Pressed on the offense's struggles, he cited stalled drives, second-down failures, and false starts in the first 20 minutes. He said Bo Nix was under heavy pressure but was still playing well. On Courtland Sutton, he said the staff must find ways to get him out of the rotation and that several things aren't clicking yet. He praised RJ Harvey's ten catches, crediting some soft coverage by the defense and some big plays he made himself. Payton also gave no injury report, saying the defense was affected when both corners were down entering the second half, and that a receiver who left early was not a major loss. He did not say whether he would have gone for it on fourth down earlier.

title: Campbell on Week 4 performance
headline: Lions lost a late-game chance vs. Carolina; Goff praised for downfield throws, but Campbell says defense and discipline must improve (no takeaways, run game leaks, penalties).
summary: Campbell praised Carolina for showing up and said the Lions fell into a two-score hole, with penalties in critical moments hurting them. He said the defense failed to cover early and gave up RPO-driven plays and then run yards in the second half, which opened up the passing game. He stressed the lack of takeaways as a major problem and said the team has to force them. He called the performance not good enough and said effort and discipline were his main focus, and he would review the tape. Campbell said he has tweaked the defense each week, has schematic options he has not yet used, and will exhaust them rather than panic at 2-2 with 13 games left. He took personal responsibility for the discipline problems, saying he has not coached it well enough. On offense, he said the team has to start faster and be more efficient, and he credited Goff for stepping up with some key throws, including downfield shots.

signals.note: Campbell credited Goff for key deep throws and the Lions' plan to stretch the field, supporting upside for the passing game.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Tank Dell, Defensive Fixes & Titans Week | Full Q&A
headline: Tank Dell, Braden Smith, and Kayden McDonald's practice windows open this week, so their Titans-week availability is the key fantasy watch; Kenneth Murray left Sunday with a concussion and no update was given.
summary: Ryans called the defense's struggles a technique and communication problem, not a scheme problem, and said the team has not done enough to earn a win. He stressed complementary football, citing special teams giving up explosives and a touchdown in the second half as a key failure. On offense he praised the game plan, the emphasis on winning first down, and C.J. Stroud's play, while saying the run blocking needs to finish better. He said the team expects to open the 21-day practice window this week for Tank Dell, Braden Smith, and Kayden McDonald, and that how they respond in practice will determine Sunday. He praised Kenneth Murray's preparation as the green-dot communicator but said Murray left the game with a concussion. Asked about the defense's bump-and-run usage for Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter, he said the team runs all those coverages without directly explaining the reduced press usage. He called penalties a mix of unavoidable bang-bang plays and controllable mistakes, citing pre-snap and alignment issues on special teams and offense. The next opponent is the Tennessee Titans.

title: Andy Reid: '[It Was a] Hard-Fought Battle Against a Good Football Team' | Postgame Press Conference - NFL Week 4
headline: Tyquan Thornton left with an ankle injury that doesn't look good, Rashee Rice tweaked a hamstring, and Kenneth Walker III earned Reid's trust on all downs after a 76-yard run.
summary: Reid opened by saying Tyquan Thornton's ankle injury "doesn't look good," with Thornton flying back with the team for further evaluation, and that Rashee Rice tweaked his hamstring. He credited the next men up at receiver for keeping the offense moving. He praised the Raiders and their coach Klint Kubiak as a tough AFC rival that will take four quarters to beat. He said the offense cleaned up its first-half problems, and he gave Kenneth Walker III high marks for a productive day, including the 76-yard run. Reid said he is comfortable giving Walker the ball on any down, and he admitted he could have called more runs. He credited Patrick Mahomes with two touchdown throws and said he trusts him in big moments, and he said Xavier Worthy was playing good football and had more chances. On defense, he praised the 72 rushing yards allowed and the work of defensive coordinator Spags, and he called special teams the best phase of the day, highlighted by Jack Cochrane's forced fumble on a Bosa kickoff and Emmett Johnson's punt catch and return. Reid said the Kingsley Suamataia situation is between him and the player and declined to elaborate. He closed by noting the upcoming bye week and a tough Chargers game afterward.

title: Sean McVay, Byron Young & Kobie Turner discuss the Rams' Week 4 win over the Eagles, riding momentum into Monday Night Football & more
headline: Puka Nacua came out of the Eagles game feeling healthy, while Terrance Ferguson is on IR for at least four games and Aaron Donald is trending toward playing Monday against Buffalo.
summary: McVay said the Rams' Week 4 win at Philadelphia was built on late execution, even though the offense was inconsistent for much of the game. He credited the defense's fourth-down stop and its pressure for keeping the Rams in the game, and said the penalties and procedural mistakes need to be cleaned up. Puka Nacua was a key factor late, and McVay said he felt healthy after the game despite a hip concern raised by reporters. Aaron Donald is trending toward practicing and playing this week, though McVay would not commit. Terrance Ferguson was placed on IR for a medial ankle sprain, and McVay expects him back before season's end. McVay said Jaylen Watson's shoulder is improving and he is expected to be ready for Buffalo if practice goes well. On special teams, McVay called the return game and coverage inconsistent, with a costly long punt return and a missed field goal among the problems. The next game is Monday Night Football against the Bills, and McVay said the offense must play cleaner against Josh Allen's group.

headline: Harbaugh says three backs will keep rotating after the Seahawks loss, so Omarion Hampton's workload stays uncertain, and he gave no injury updates on Rashawn Slater or Joe Alt.
summary: Harbaugh credited his players' fight and never-say-die attitude after a loss to Seattle, but he gave few concrete answers. He said three running backs are playing well and rotating carries, and he called that the best approach for the team without explaining why it began in Week 3. He praised Justin Herbert's competitiveness and grit and said he respects no quarterback more, while saying he could not speak to Herbert's comfort in the offense in the first half. He pointed to four young offensive linemen who played in the game, including Jake Slaughter moving to guard, and said he was proud of how they fought. He rejected the idea that offensive coordinator Mike's job was in jeopardy and said the staff would keep adjusting and growing. He said the fourth-quarter drives were a good sign and that the offense simply needed to keep playing without worrying. On injuries he gave no update on Rashawn Slater or Joe Alt and said he did not know Herbert's health status after taking many hits.

headline: Jalen Nailor has a concussion; Kubiak has no answer yet on the run game, and the tight end group drew praise.
summary: Kubiak opened by saying Jalen Nailor has a concussion and praised his team's effort in a loss to Kansas City. He said the team was aggressive by design, and he didn't regret going for it on fourth down, but it didn't convert. He took responsibility for a late-game problem: the play call came in too slowly, and he admitted a legal-shift issue and a missed opportunity. He credited the Chiefs, saying they were well coached and made big plays. Asked about the run game, he said the team must find the answer, citing good backs and a good offensive line, but didn't offer a specific fix. He also praised Kirk Cousins for a strong performance and the tight end group for its production, and he said the team will move on to New England.

injuries.detail: Kubiak said Nailor has a concussion. No timeline or practice status was given.

signals.claim: Has a concussion; availability for the New England game was not addressed.
signals.note: A concussion can keep a receiver out for an extended period, which cuts into his weekly fantasy value until he clears the protocol.
signals.quote: Jalen Nailor has a concussion.

signals.note: Kubiak praised Cousins's late-game leadership and play, which supports his continued starting role.
signals.quote: He played a really good football tonight.

signals.claim: The tight end group will keep being counted on every week.
signals.note: Kubiak singled out the tight end group after it produced over 100 yards and two touchdowns, which points to continued heavy target share.
signals.quote: we count on them every week.

topics.detail: Kubiak said the team has to find an answer to get the run game going consistently, and he gave no specific plan. He acknowledged the backs and offensive line are good enough and that there is more to develop.

topics.topic: Late-game play call and fourth-down decisions
topics.detail: Kubiak said he didn't get the play call in fast enough at the end of the game and called it a missed opportunity. He defended the decision to go for it on fourth down, though he regretted not converting.
Kubiak acknowledged the team gave Kansas City too many opportunities, a minus-two turnover margin after a strong takeaway year.
Kubiak called the tight end room an impressive group, with Brock Bowers and others credited for the 100-plus yards and two touchdowns.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 5, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley's hamstring injury leaves his Sunday availability uncertain. Sirianni will update on Wednesday.
summary: Sirianni said Saquon Barkley's availability for Sunday is still unknown after his hamstring injury, and that the team will have more answers by Wednesday as players respond to treatment. He said Barkley will do everything he can to return. On the offense, he said the team still hasn't settled on an identity, and the mix of under-center and gun sets reflects game-plan needs rather than a settled personnel decision. He acknowledged the goal-line and short-yardage failures (a fourth-and-one and a third-and-goal from the two) and said the tape review is about accountability and finding solutions. He gave no update on Lane Johnson's return. He praised rookie tackle Markel Bell's performance as solid, with good movement on double teams and second-level blocks, while noting he wasn't perfect. He said left guard Cam is doing good things and there is no plan to change him. On pass protection, he declined to say who makes the protection calls, called the breakdowns multiple factors including coaching and matchups, and said it has to be more consistent. He said the team will leave for the international trip on Friday to get a full week of practice in, and that jet lag was part of the planning.

injuries.detail: Hamstring injury; availability for Sunday unknown. Sirianni said more information would come Wednesday, and he expects Barkley to do everything possible to return.
No update given on his status or expected return to the building.

signals.claim: Availability for Sunday is undetermined; team will update on Wednesday
signals.note: The RB1 timeline is uncertain, so backups and the expected workload could change sharply depending on Wednesday's update.

signals.claim: Played well as a rookie tackle on short notice and was praised by the coach
signals.note: Positive reviews of a rookie filling in on short notice suggest he has earned continued reps on the line.
signals.quote: I thought he was solid.

topics.detail: Sirianni said the team is still searching for its identity, that under-center versus gun formations depend on the game plan, and that the team needs to be able to do multiple things. He said consistency has been lacking in both coaching and playing.
The offense failed on a fourth-and-one and a third-down attempt from the two-yard line. Sirianni said the film review will look for solutions and that the issue has more than one cause.
Sirianni declined to name who makes protection calls, calling it a set process. He acknowledged protection breakdowns, including losing matchups and blitz pickups, and said the team must improve.
The team will leave Friday for the international trip to London, to allow a full week of practice. Sirianni said the decision came from research and that jet lag was considered.
Sirianni said the team feels good about the players who step in and take reps, and he does not treat injuries as an excuse.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald On The 30-23 Win vs. Chargers
headline: Nick Emmanwori should be fully back, Leonard Williams' ankle doesn't look serious, and Sam Darnold is cleared after taking too many hits.
summary: Macdonald called the 3-1 start something to be grateful for but said the Seahawks are not yet playing to their standard. He said the team has much room to improve in ball security and penalties, and that seven personal fouls were unacceptable. He described a 24-to-48-hour process to address discipline, separating normal aggressive penalties from selfish ones. He praised the run game, including Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, and said getting Rashid Shaheed going, including a touchdown on a called play, was great. He credited the defense for staying together to close the game, though he wants better end-of-half execution. On injuries, he said Leonard Williams has an ankle issue that doesn't look serious, Nick Emmanwori should be fully back, and Sam Darnold played tough and is ready to go despite too many quarterback hits. He also said Ty has a shot to play next week, and he gave no timeline for the player placed on injured reserve. He said the staff must find ways to get deserving players like Drake Thomas, Nehemiah Pritchett and Trevon Diggs on the field.

title: Kyle Shanahan Talks 49ers Win Over Broncos, Moves to 4-0
headline: Kittle looks fully back from his Achilles, Deebo Samuel was huge in the run game, and Dre Greenlaw led the team in tackles; Upton Stout's shoulder/AC injury is still unclear.
summary: Shanahan said the game played out much like the team expected, with a physical, low-scoring stretch and a plan to run the ball heavily. He credited a special teams turnover that changed the momentum, and said the offense struggled early on short-yardage plays before getting going in the second half with better drives. He praised the defense for keeping the game manageable and said the team never felt it had to panic. On injuries, he said Upton Stout likely has an AC-type injury to the shoulder but won't know more until tomorrow, and an unnamed player with a knee injury is probably a sprain with the ACL looking intact. Fred Warner dealt with stomach issues early but was fine. Shanahan said Mike Evans played through significant rib pain and was impressive. He was glad to have Dre Greenlaw back at home and said Greenlaw held his emotions in check while leading the team in tackles. He said George Kittle has looked unbelievable since returning from his Achilles injury and that his conditioning, not his health, was the main concern early on. Brock Purdy improved after a rough start, and Shanahan said he told him to stop throwing incompletions. Deebo Samuel was big both as a runner and as a receiver on key short catches. The team now heads to Seattle next week.
